verdict.rationale: AMD documents its own SDK stack for this chip: Ryzen AI Software with ONNX Runtime and the Vitis AI EP through C++ and Python APIs, the Lemonade SDK for LLMs, C++ CVML library APIs, the Quark quantization toolkit and the GAIA agent framework. Code samples and a language-agnostic server interface back this up. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on community corroboration of building with the official SDKs (community reports mention only llama.cpp).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs

citations.quote: The AI model is deployed using the ONNX Runtime with either C++ or Python APIs.
the Lemonade SDK, which is multi-vendor open-source software that provides everything necessary for quickly getting started with LLMs on OGA or llama.cpp
Each Ryzen AI CVML library feature offers a simple C++ application programming interface (API) that can be easily incorporated into existing applications.
This allows applications written in any language (C#, JavaScript, Python, C++, etc.) to easily integrate with Ryzen AI LLMs.
This allows developers to build and deploy models trained in PyTorch or TensorFlow and run them directly on laptops powered by Ryzen AI using ONNX Runtime and the Vitis™ AI Execution Provider (EP).
